# DSH Session Migration

> A button in the DeepSeek Harness session header that moves a whole session — log,
> `header.cwd`,

and workspace membership — into another working directory, with session
> browsing, one-click backup
export, and a workspace health check.
English | 中文
## Why a tool is needed
A DSH session's workspace membership is decided by **three** things:
| # | Where | What |
| ① | `~/.dsh/sessions/<projectKey(cwd)>/<sessionId>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd` | the directory name enc

odes the working directory |
| ② | the header in **frame 1** of the log | the `cwd` is stored again

inside the log |
| ③ | `~/.dsh/storages/workspace.json` → `workspace.sessionIds` | decides which wor
| ③ | `~/.dsh/storages/workspace.json` → `workspace.sessionIds` | decides which workspace lists it |
Moving the folder by hand trips one of three real crash modes:
- **A** — two copies of one `sessionId` (copy instead of move): the start-up scan conflicts and the

session list scrambles.
- **B** — a registry entry pointing at data that is gone: **the whole worksp

ace refuses to open**, and `directoryPickerController` goes unavailable with it.
- **C** — editing `
workspace.json` while DSH runs: the in-memory registry overwrites it on exit, so changes are half-ap
ace.json` while DSH runs: the in-memory registry overwrites it on exit, so changes are half-applied.

This plugin performs the flow behind one button, and uses only DSH's own services and
(byte-exact) s

torage conventions: move, never copy; rewrite only frame 1; write the
registry only through the live
`workspaceRegistry` Service.
## Features
- **Migrate a session** to an existing workspace or any browsed directory: preflight first, then exe
cute, with an automatic backup, byte-level verification, automatic rollback, and copy-paste rollback

commands.
- **Optionally move the source working-directory files** into the target (top-level entri
es; a name clash is a refusal; the old directory stays as an empty directory so other sessions keep

working).
- **Session list**: id, working directory, log size, frame count, last write, current memb

ership, and problem badges.
- **Health check**: dangling references, duplicate ids, header/directory
mismatch, empty logs, missing workspace directories, unregistered sessions. Dangling references can

be removed safely through the live registry — no shutdown needed.
- **Export a backup**: copy the s
ession directory to a destination of your choice, with a `migration-export.json` manifest, without t
ouching the registry.

The browser half is picked up automatically from the `dsh.client` declaration.
**If the button does

not appear, reload the page once** — a freshly installed client
bundle needs the page to walk the mo

d the page once** — a freshly installed client
bundle needs the page to walk the module graph again.
## Usage

1. Open any session; an icon button (two panels, one arrow) appears in the header utilities.
2. Pick
the session to migrate in the left column. **The session currently in use cannot migrate itself** —

its log is open, so the plugin refuses.
3. Pick a target workspace, or switch to "custom path" and

type/browse any directory.
4. Read the preflight: project-key change, target session directory, whet

her the workspace will be created, and the file-move entry count and clashes.
5. Click “Start migrat

ion”, then “Confirm migration”.
6. The result lists each step: backup → data move → header rewrite →
verification → file move → workspace membership.
### About “restart required”
The workspace step reports `pending-restart` by design, not as a failure:

> The live workspace registry is a start-up snapshot indexed from session headers; a plugin
> cannot

refresh it in place, and writing `workspace.json` by hand while DSH runs is crash
> mode C.

So the membership write goes into a queue
(`~/.dsh/plugin-data/dsh-session-migration/pending.json`)

and is applied **on the next DSH
start**, with the outcome logged. Nothing to do manually: restart o

nce and the session
appears under its new workspace. The “Pending” tab can retry it sooner.
## Safety model
| Invariant | How |
| Move, never copy | an existing target session directory is a refusal; the target log size is verif

ied after the move |
| No dangling registry references | the registry is written only through `works

paceRegistry`, and only after the data is in place |
| Only frame 1 changes | decompress frame 1, se

t `cwd`, recompress frame 1, concatenate the untouched tail |
| Verifiable integrity | compare every

thing **after frame 1**; a growing frame count (chat continues) is not a failure |
| Idempotent | a

repeated move to the same target is a `same-target` no-op, never a second copy |
| Rollback | any fa
ilure moves data back, restores the `.bak`, removes a created workspace, and prints copy-paste rollb

ack commands |
| No self-migration | liveness comes from the `agents` Service; a live session is ref

mmands |
| No self-migration | liveness comes from the `agents` Service; a live session is refused |
### Why "decompress, edit, recompress" is wrong

`zlib.zstdDecompressSync(log)` returns **only the first frame** — normally the ~200-byte
header. Tha

t looks like “the whole log is one line”, and code that concludes the session is
empty or corrupt ca

n delete real history. This plugin therefore walks RFC 8878
frame/block headers for exact frame boun

daries (falling back to a magic-byte scan), counts
frames in chunks without loading an 18 MB log int
o memory, and replaces frame 1 only.
## Health checks
| code | severity | meaning | auto-fix |

| `dangling-reference` | error | the registry names a session that is not on disk | ✅ one click |
|
`duplicate-session` | error | the same sessionId exists under several project keys | ❌ keep the newe

r one, back up the other |
| `cwd-mismatch` | error | `header.cwd` disagrees with the project direct

ory | ❌ manual |
| `id-mismatch` | error | directory name ≠ `header.id` | ❌ manual |
